papers.title_zh: 聚乙二醇化干扰素 α-2b 添加到核苷(酸)类似物可减少肝细胞癌和晚期纤维化的失代偿 慢性乙型肝炎
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND The current therapeutic strategy of adding pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) is primarily aimed at achieving functional cure. However, its value in improving prognosis and the suitable candidates for this combination strategy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis remain to be further explored. AIM To evaluate the long-term prognosis benefit of add-on Peg-IFNα-2b therapy in patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. METHODS This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients diagnosed with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. Participants were divided into two groups: (1) Those receiving combination therapy (Peg-IFNα-2b add-on to ongoing NA treatment); and (2) Those receiving NA monotherapy. A 1:1 propensity score matching approach was applied to balance baseline characteristics between groups. In survival analysis, the outcomes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and decompensated cirrhosis were stratified by baseline clinical features and established HCC risk scores. RESULTS The analysis included 302 matched pairs, with a median follow-up duration of 220 weeks. Combination therapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of developing HCC (hazard ratio = 0.22; 95%CI: 0.11-0.48) and decompensated cirrhosis (hazard ratio = 0.39; 95%CI: 0.20-0.77) than NA monotherapy. These benefits were particularly pronounced among patients classified as intermediate-to-high risk by validated HCC prediction models and in those with persistent biochemical abnormalities lasting > 12 months. CONCLUSION Add-on therapy with Peg-IFNα-2b to NAs is significantly associated with reduced HCC and decompensation in high-risk patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, supporting its use in this population.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景目前在核苷(酸)类似物(NA)中添加聚乙二醇化干扰素(Peg-IFN)α-2b的治疗策略主要旨在实现功能性治愈。然而,其在改善 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关晚期纤维化或代偿性肝硬化患者预后方面的价值以及该联合策略的合适候选者仍有待进一步探索。目的 评估附加 Peg-IFNα-2b 治疗对 HBV 相关晚期纤维化或代偿性肝硬化患者的长期预后益处。方法 这项回顾性 队列研究 研究纳入了诊断为 HBV 相关晚期纤维化或代偿性肝硬化的患者。参与者被分为两组:(1)接受联合治疗(Peg-IFNα-2b 附加到正在进行的 NA 治疗);(2) 接受 NA 单一疗法的患者。采用 1:1 倾向评分匹配方法来平衡各组之间的基线特征。在生存分析中,肝细胞癌 (HCC) 和失代偿性肝硬化的结果根据基线临床特征和既定的 HCC 风险评分进行分层。结果 该分析包括 302 对配对,中位随访时间为 220 周。与 NA 单一疗法相比,联合治疗与发生 HCC(风险比 = 0.22;95% CI:0.11-0.48)和失代偿性肝硬化(风险比 = 0.39;95% CI:0.20-0.77)的风险显着降低相关。这些益处在经验证的 HCC 预测模型分类为中高风险的患者以及持续生化异常持续 > 12 个月的患者中尤其明显。结论 Peg-IFNα-2b 与 NA 的附加治疗与患有 HBV 相关晚期纤维化或肝硬化的高危患者的 HCC 减少和失代偿显着相关,支持其在该人群中的使用。

papers.title: Association of IL-10 (rs1800896) Gene Polymorphism and Serum IL-10 Levels with Chronic Hepatitis B Infection
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a main general validity threat. It evolves under the influence of various factors, including immunogenetic ones. This study assessed the correlation between the occurrence of interleukin 10 gene (IL10) polymorphisms and the development of these infections. This retrospective case control study 64 chronic HBV infections, 39 HBV clearance groups and 31 controls. "Tetra-primer ARMS-PCR" is a technique that used to study the single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) at IL10 promoter (-1082A>G; rs1800896). The IL-10 levels were determined in patients with chronic HBV infections, HBV clearance and control group by using an Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA). Based on allele polymorphism analysis, three genotypes were identified: AA (46.8 %), AG (43.7 %) and GG (9.3 %). The level of IL10 in HBV patients was significantly greater than that in other sets. In addition, these findings indicate that polymorphism may not affect initial infection but rather disease progression or disease immune response.
papers.journal: Journal of Wasit for Science and Medicine

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between IL-10 gene polymorphisms and chronic hepatitis B infection. It conducted a retrospective case control study involving 64 chronic HBV infections, 39 HBV clearance groups, and 31 controls. The methods included Tetra-primer ARMS-PCR for SNP analysis and ELISA for measuring IL-10 levels. Results showed three genotypes (AA, AG, GG) with varying frequencies, and significantly higher IL-10 levels in HBV patients compared to other groups. papers.title: Translational Multiplexed Raman Pathological Imaging for Precise Diagnosis of HBV-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Multiplexed vibrational imaging holds great potential for tissue molecular analysis, yet fully standardized workflows suitable for routine clinical histopathology remain scarce. Herein, we report a clinically applicable methodology using monodisperse triple-bond Raman polymer nanoparticles (∼50 nm). This approach integrates one-step labeling and single-scan acquisition to achieve high-performance multiplexed Raman imaging of 5 protein markers in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues. Targeting hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated HCC, our biomarker panel combines the viral protein HBx with 4 clinically used indicators: AFP, GS, GPC3, and CD34. We further reveal a clinically critical dissociation: several high-grade HBV-HCC specimens exhibit markedly elevated oncogenic markers with comparatively low HBx expression, consistent with antiviral therapy suppressing viral protein production without reversing tumor aggressiveness. Taking advantage of the ultranarrow, well-resolved signals generated by triple-bond tags within the biological silent region (1800−2800 cm−1), we achieve high-fidelity spatial mapping and quantitative analysis. Unlike conventional pathological methods relying on morphological observation, clinical manifestations, or single-marker detection, this technique simultaneously evaluates viral etiology, tumor progression, and metastatic potential, effectively reducing misclassification risk in patients with discordant viral and oncogenic profiles, and completes the entire assay within approximately 24 h. This study establishes a rapid and reliable histopathological platform that integrates pathogen identification and comprehensive cancer characterization, demonstrating substantial value for both cancer research and clinical diagnostics.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:多重振动成像在组织分子分析方面具有巨大潜力,但适合常规临床组织病理学的完全标准化工作流程仍然很少。在此,我们报告了一种使用单分散三键拉曼聚合物纳米颗粒(∼50 nm)的临床适用方法。该方法集成了一步标记和单次扫描采集,可实现肝细胞癌 (HCC) 组织中 5 种蛋白质标记物的高性能多重拉曼成像。针对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关 HCC,我们的生物标志物组合将病毒蛋白 HBx 与 4 个临床使用的指标相结合:AFP、GS、GPC3 和 CD34。我们进一步揭示了临床上关键的分离:几个高级别 HBV-HCC 标本表现出显着升高的致癌标志物,而 HBx 表达相对较低,这与 抗病毒药物 疗法抑制病毒蛋白产生而不逆转肿瘤侵袭性一致。利用生物沉默区域(1800−2800 cm−1)内三键标签产生的超窄、高分辨率信号,我们实现了高保真空间映射和定量分析。与依赖形态学观察、临床表现或单标志物检测的传统病理方法不同,该技术同时评估病毒病原学、肿瘤进展和转移潜力,有效降低病毒和致癌谱不一致患者的错误分类风险,并在约24小时内完成整个检测。这项研究建立了一个快速、可靠的组织病理学平台,整合了病原体识别和全面的癌症表征,展示了对癌症研究和临床诊断的巨大价值。

papers.title: Metabolomics reveals metabolite profiles associated with clinical cure of chronic HBV infection under different drug interventions
papers.abstract: Objectives: To identify differential metabolites associated with complete cure in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with various regimens of entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha. Methods: The retrospective, case-control study was conducted at the Mudan People's Hospital of Heze, Shandong, China, and comprised samples from the institutional laboratory department of hepatitis B virus patients enrolled between June 2, 2021, and December 30, 2023. The patients were grouped based on the treatment protocol and the evidence of complete cure. Groups A and B comprised patients who were and were not clinically cured after receiving 48 weeks of sequential entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha. Group E patients received entecavir monotherapy for over 2 years without a clinical cure, and group W included untreated patients. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify differential metabolites associated with clinical cure in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha. Conducted at Mudan People's Hospital in China, it involved a retrospective case-control design with patients grouped based on treatment and cure status. Kaempferide and other metabolites showed significant fold-change values, suggesting their potential role in clinical cure. The results may help develop biomarkers for treatment monitoring. However, the study's retrospective nature and small sample size limit its generalisability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Pilot Model for Newly Diagnosed in-Hospital Bacterial and Fungal Infections in Decompensated Hepatitis B Cirrhosis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Background and Aims: Recognizing infection risk during hospitalization is important in decompensated cirrhosis, although routine measurements may reflect infection already developing. We developed and internally validated an admission-time pilot model for newly diagnosed in-hospital bacterial or fungal infection in decompensated hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 150 patients admitted in 2023– 2025. Admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score (MELD) were fixed as predictors for the primary Firth/Jeffreys penalized logistic model. Complete-case analysis included 148 patients and 20 events. We refitted the fixed model in 1000 bootstrap samples, assessed calibration and discrimination, and examined early-event exclusions and an admission-only ridge model. The hospital-recorded procedure variable was excluded from prediction. Secondary analyses used Aalen–Johansen cumulative incidence, Fine–Gray regression and cause-specific Cox, with infection-free discharge and death as competing events. Results: Among 148 modeled patients, the NLR and MELD odds ratios were 1.073 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.025– 1.124) and 1.062 (95% CI, 1.002– 1.125). Apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.716 versus 0.633 for MELD alone. Optimism-corrected AUC was 0.700 (approximate 95% CI 0.566– 0.846), corrected Brier score was 0.103, and corrected calibration slope was 0.981 (approximate bootstrap interval 0.506– 1.646). AUCs after separate exclusions of infections recorded by hospital day 2 or day 3 were 0.750 and 0.731, respectively. Fine–Gray subdistribution hazard ratios were 1.069 (95% CI 1.042– 1.098) for NLR and 1.064 (1.021– 1.109) for MELD. Conclusion: This admission model showed modest discrimination with imprecise calibration. Retrospective ascertainment and limited validation preclude clinical use. Prospective external validation at a defined prediction time and horizon is needed before the model guides surveillance or treatment. Keywords: hepatitis B, decompensated cirrhosis, infection, prediction model, internal validation, nomogram

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a pilot model for predicting newly diagnosed in-hospital bacterial or fungal infections in patients with decompensated hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis. A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from 150 patients admitted between 2023 and 2025. The model incorporated admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) scores as predictors. Results showed modest discrimination with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.716, and imprecise calibration. The study concluded that the model requires prospective external validation before it can be used in clinical practice. The findings suggest that further research is needed to improve the model's accuracy and applicability for surveillance and treatment decisions in patients with HBV-related cirrhosis.

papers.title: Epidemiology of Hepatitis B and C Viral Infections Among Tuberculosis Patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis patients coinfected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV) may be particularly vulnerable to liver injury during treatment. Evidence on the burden and clinical implications of these infections in Ebonyi State remains limited. The aim of the study is to assess the epidemiology of Hepatitis B and C Viruses Infection among tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to (i) determine the prevalence of HBV, HCV, and HBV/HCV co-infection among tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, (ii) to identify common risk factors among co-infected TB-patients with viral hepatitis B and C in Ebonyi State. (iii) to determine the knowledge, attitude and practice of TB patients towards HBV and HCV infections. This study assessed HBV/HCV prevalence, risk factors, and patients’ knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP).
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

papers.title: Immune Response to Hepatitis B Vaccination According to National EPI Schedule among Children Below 2 Years
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus infection is a public health burden globally. We incorporate Hep-B vaccine in our EPI schedule. There is no comprehensive data regarding the immune response of the HBV vaccine at one year in our country. The study was done to assess the immune response among HBV vaccinated children at this age group. Materials and methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at EPI outdoor of Chittagong Medical College Hospital from January to December, 2022. Blood sample from 375 vaccinated children were tested for Anti-HBs titre by ELISA technique in between 9 months to 15 months. Statistical analyses were performed with Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 23.0. Results: This study shows that older children and male tend to have better immune responses after vaccination and malnutrition is a significant risk factor for low antibody titers. This study also shows that 79.2% of children had satisfactory or high levels of anti-HBs antibodies (≥10 mIU/mL). However, 20.8% of children had low antibody titers ( <10 mIU/mL) indicating inadequate immune protection. Conclusion: Most children vaccinated under the current EPI schedule develop protective immunity against hepatitis B; a small proportion remain vulnerable due to inadequate seroconversion. Chatt Maa Shi Hosp Med Coll J; Vol.25 (2); July 2026; Page 10-15
papers.journal: Chattagram Maa-O-Shishu Hospital Medical College Journal

papers.title: Intrinsic replication advantage of a Hepatitis B Virus genotype C strain is independent of the basal core promoter A1762T/G1764A mutation
papers.abstract: This study aimed to isolate and characterize individual hepatitis B virus (HBV) strains from a patient co-infected with genotype B and C, and to directly compare their intrinsic replication capacities. HBV DNA was isolated from a chronic hepatitis B patient. Genotypes were determined by genotype-specific polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and full-length genomes were cloned. Two clones representing subgenotype B2 (c17) and C1 (c21) were selected, sequenced and transfected into HepG2 cells. Viral replication was assessed via Southern blot and quantitative PCR. The role of the common Adenine (A)1762Thymine (T/)Guanine (G)1764A mutation in the C1 clone was investigated by site-directed mutagenesis. As a result, the genotype C1 clone exhibited significantly higher replication capacity than the B2 clone. Counterintuitively, reverting the A1762T/G1764A mutation in the C1 clone to wild-type further enhanced its replication, indicating this mutation was not the primary driver of its high replicative fitness. In conclusion, HBV genotype C1 possesses a greater inherent replication capacity than B2, independent of the classic basal core promoter (BCP) mutation, providing a virological explanation for its association with severe disease outcomes in co-infection.

papers.title: Autophagy-related gene expression is associated with fibrosis severity in chronic hepatitis B and fatty liver disease
papers.abstract: Autophagy regulates hepatocyte survival, stellate cell activation and inflammation, but its transcriptional correlates in human liver fibrosis are poorly defined. In liver biopsy transcriptomes from 124 patients with chronic hepatitis B, 20 autophagy-related genes differed nominally between fibrotic and non-fibrotic tissue. Co-expression network analysis prioritized CCL2 , MYC , CDKN1A and CAPN2 , whose expression correlated with immune cell signatures and was positively associated with fibrosis stage after adjustment for inflammation grade, age and sex. An exploratory 15-gene neural-network classifier had an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.982; bootstrap validation of a re-implemented development procedure gave an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.865, and the classifier had an AUC of 0.833 (95% confidence interval, 0.556–1.000) in whole blood from six healthy individuals and six with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. In two independent cohorts with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, expression of CCL2 , CAPN2 and CDKN1A , but not MYC , was higher in advanced than in mild fibrosis (n = 72), and that of all four genes was higher in fibrotic than in non-fibrotic liver (n = 112), largely owing to cirrhotic samples. These genes warrant further study as markers of fibrosis severity; their cellular sources and roles in fibrosis are unknown.

Co-expression network analysis prioritized CCL2 , MYC , CDKN1A and CAPN2 , whose expression correlated with immune cell signatures and was positively associated with fibrosis stage after adjustment for inflammation grade, age and sex. An exploratory 15-gene neural-network classifier had an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.982; bootstrap validation of a re-implemented development procedure gave an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.865, and the classifier had an AUC of 0.833 (95% confidence interval, 0.556–1.000) in whole blood from six healthy individuals and six with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. In two independent cohorts with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, expression of CCL2 , CAPN2 and CDKN1A , but not MYC , was higher in advanced than in mild fibrosis (n = 72), and that of all four genes was higher in fibrotic than in non-fibrotic liver (n = 112), largely owing to cirrhotic samples. These genes warrant further study as markers of fibrosis severity; their cellular sources and roles in fibrosis are unknown.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在研究自噬在人类肝纤维化中的转录相关性,因为自噬在肝细胞存活、星状细胞活化和炎症中的作用已得到充分证实,但其与纤维化严重程度的关系仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 124 名 慢性乙型肝炎 患者的肝活检转录组,确定了 20 个自噬相关基因,这些基因在纤维化组织和非纤维化组织之间存在显着差异。它还检查了两名患有非酒精性脂肪肝的独立 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员进行了共表达网络分析来对基因进行优先排序,并使用引导方法开发和验证了探索性 15 基因神经网络分类器。
elements_zh.main_results: 分类器的接收者操作特征曲线 (AUC) 下的表观面积为 0.982,但重新实施的开发程序的引导验证给出的乐观校正 AUC 为 0.865。在来自 6 名健康个体和 6 名乙型肝炎相关肝硬化患者的全血中,分类器的 AUC 为 0.833(95% 置信区间,0.556-1.000)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,CCL2、CAPN2 和 CDKN1A 可能作为纤维化严重程度的潜在标志物,尽管它们的细胞来源和在纤维化中的作用仍不清楚。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些基因可以为未来纤维化严重程度标记物的研究提供信息,可能有助于开发与乙型肝炎相关的肝脏疾病的诊断工具。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于使用探索性分类器以及健康个体和肝硬化患者的样本量较小而受到限制,导致置信度评估适中。

papers.title: Peripheral Blood Natural Killer Cell Quantity, Phenotype, and Function Across the Clinical Spectrum of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: This scoping review aims to systematically map and critically examine the available evidence on the quantity, phenotype, and function of peripheral blood natural killer (NK) cells across the clinical spectrum of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including chronic HBV infection and hepatitis, HBV-related liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, and HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although NK cells contribute to antiviral immunity, immune regulation, and tumor surveillance, findings concerning their circulating frequency, phenotypic characteristics, and functional responses remain heterogeneous. Differences in clinical populations, disease classification, antiviral treatment, blood sample processing, flow cytometric gating strategies, measurement denominators, and functional assay conditions may limit direct comparisons between studies. The review will be guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), with additional attention to transparent reporting of literature searches using PRISMA-S. Eligible evidence will primarily comprise original human studies reporting at least one peripheral blood NK-cell outcome related to quantity, phenotype, or function in populations with chronic HBV infection or HBV-associated liver disease. Studies involving mixed HCC etiologies will be considered for HBV-specific synthesis only where relevant subgroup findings can be identified separately. Peripheral blood findings will be distinguished from intrahepatic and tumor-infiltrating NK-cell measurements. The review will map NK-cell frequencies and absolute counts, CD56bright and CD56dim subsets, activating and inhibitory receptor profiles, and functional measurements such as cytokine production, degranulation, cytotoxicity, and antibody-dependent responses. Particular attention will be given to whether quantitative and functional outcomes were assessed in comparable populations, at the same time points, and under sufficiently similar experimental conditions. Preliminary literature searching, bibliographic data collection, deduplication, and targeted examination of selected publications have already been undertaken before registration. The registration will document the current stage of the review and specify the procedures for subsequent study selection, data charting, evidence synthesis, and protocol amendments. Earlier activities will not be represented as prospectively preregistered. Artificial intelligence tools have assisted with preliminary bibliographic organization, methodological planning, and exploration of the literature. Their use will be documented transparently. Decisions concerning study eligibility, extracted evidence, interpretation, and final conclusions will remain subject to human review and verification against original sources. The anticipated outcome is an evidence map identifying the distribution of research across HBV-related clinical conditions, the extent to which NK-cell quantity, phenotype, and function have been examined, major sources of methodological heterogeneity, and areas where evidence is limited or insufficiently comparable. The findings are intended to inform future clinical immunology and hepatology research and the design of more standardized investigations of peripheral blood NK cells in HBV-associated liver disease.

papers.abstract_zh: 本次范围审查旨在系统地绘制和严格审查关于 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染临床谱中外周血自然杀伤 (NK) 细胞的数量、表型和功能的现有证据,包括慢性 HBV 感染和肝炎、HBV 相关的肝纤维化和肝硬化以及 HBV 相关的肝细胞癌 (HCC)。尽管 NK 细胞有助于 抗病毒药物 免疫、免疫调节和肿瘤 监测,但有关其循环频率、表型特征和功能反应的研究结果仍然存在异质性。临床人群、疾病分类、抗病毒药物 治疗、血样处理、流式细胞术门控策略、测量分母和功能测定条件的差异可能会限制研究之间的直接比较。该审查将以 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) 范围界定审查方法为指导,并根据 PRISMA 范围界定审查扩展 (PRISMA-ScR) 进行报告,同时额外关注使用 PRISMA-S 进行文献检索的透明报告。合格的证据主要包括原始人体研究,报告至少一种与慢性 HBV 感染或 HBV 相关肝病人群的数量、表型或功能相关的外周血 NK 细胞结果。只有在可以单独确定相关亚组结果的情况下,才会考虑涉及混合 HCC 病因学的研究进行 HBV 特异性合成。外周血检查结果将与肝内和肿瘤浸润 NK 细胞测量结果区分开来。该综述将绘制 NK 细胞频率和绝对计数、CD56bright 和 CD56dim 子集、激活和抑制受体谱以及功能测量(例如细胞因子产生、脱颗粒、细胞毒性和抗体依赖性反应)。将特别关注是否在可比人群、相同时间点和足够相似的实验条件下评估了定量和功能结果。注册前已对选定出版物进行了初步文献检索、书目数据收集、重复数据删除和有针对性的审查。注册将记录当前阶段的审查,并指定后续研究选择、数据图表、证据合成和方案修订的程序。早期的活动不会被视为前瞻性预注册。人工智能工具有助于初步的书目组织、方法规划和文献探索。它们的使用将被透明记录。有关研究资格、提取的证据、解释和最终结论的决定仍将接受人工审查和针对原始来源的验证。预期结果是一张证据图,确定了 HBV 相关临床状况的研究分布、NK 细胞数量、表型和功能的检查程度、方法异质性的主要来源以及证据有限或缺乏可比性的领域。这些发现旨在为未来的临床免疫学和肝病学研究以及 HBV 相关肝病中外周血 NK 细胞的更标准化研究的设计提供信息。

papers.title: Interferon therapy reduces incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with high risk of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND The proportion of patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is as high as 85.69% among HCC patients in China. Current anti-HBV drugs include nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) and interferon (IFN). AIM To compare the impact of NAs and IFN therapy on the occurrence of HCC in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC. METHODS We enrolled 368 patients with high risk of HBV-related HCC, and 120 received subcutaneous injections of IFN, with or without NAs, constituting the IFN group. The remaining 248 patients were assigned to the NAs group, and received treatment with NAs alone. RESULTS For patients with a high risk of HBV-related HCC, after a 5-year treatment period, HCC incidence in the IFN group was 2.54%, while the NAs group showed a significantly higher incidence of 25.74% (P CONCLUSION IFN-based therapy, compared with NAs, significantly reduced the risk of HCC in patients with high risk of HBV-related HCC.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the high incidence of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in China and evaluate the impact of interferon (IFN) therapy versus nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) on HCC occurrence in high-risk patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 368 patients with high risk of HBV-related HCC, with 120 patients receiving IFN therapy (with or without NAs) and 248 patients receiving NA therapy alone.
analysis.methods: Patients were enrolled and followed for a 5-year treatment period. HCC incidence was monitored and compared between the IFN group and the NAs group using statistical analysis to determine significance.
analysis.main_results: After 5 years of treatment, the HCC incidence in the IFN group was 2.54%, while the NAs group had a significantly higher incidence of 25.74% (P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that IFN-based therapy significantly reduces HCC risk compared to NAs alone in high-risk HBV patients, highlighting a novel therapeutic approach.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that IFN-based therapy could be a more effective option for reducing HCC incidence in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC, potentially informing treatment guidelines and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the clear comparison between IFN and NAs groups and the statistically significant results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of interferon (IFN) therapy versus nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC. The research aimed to address the high prevalence of HBV-related HCC in China and evaluate therapeutic efficacy. A retrospective cohort study enrolled 368 patients, with 120 receiving IFN therapy and 248 receiving NA therapy alone. After 5 years, HCC incidence was 2.54% in the IFN group and 25.74% in the NAs group (P < 0.001). The authors concluded that IFN-based therapy significantly reduces HCC risk compared to NAs alone, offering a novel therapeutic approach. These findings may inform treatment guidelines for high-risk HBV patients. The study's retrospective design introduces potential limitations, but the results are robust due to the clear comparison and statistical significance.

papers.title: Interpretability-driven feature engineering enables compact and accurate multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Clinical artificial intelligence (AI) often trades predictive performance against interpretability. This study develops an interpretability-driven feature engineering framework for multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B. A total of 36,024 hospitalization records from 22,001 patients were included. The framework integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based main and interaction effects was used to construct compact machine learning models for classifying disease non-progression, liver cirrhosis (LC), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). SHAP main effects selected the top 15 features per outcome; TreeSHAP interactions selected four pairwise terms. Performance was evaluated using patient-level data splitting, temporal validation, and independent external validation, with calibration and decision-curve analyses. The full-feature models achieved superior discrimination (AUCs: 0.927, 0.897, and 0.899) for classifying hospitalization-recorded disease non-progression, LC, and HCC, respectively. The corresponding compact models maintained strong discrimination (AUCs: 0.911, 0.882, and 0.890) with 80.8% fewer features. Interaction models yielded subtle AUC shifts (AUCs: 0.912, 0.881, and 0.891) while characterizing potential clinical joint-effect patterns. Temporal validation yielded AUCs of 0.863, 0.827, and 0.847, while external validation yielded AUCs of 0.829, 0.865, and 0.827, respectively. The framework produced compact and transparent models for contemporaneous risk stratification in clinical practice, seamlessly uniting predictive accuracy with multi-level interpretability.

analysis_zh.main_results: 全特征模型在对住院记录的疾病无进展、LC 和 HCC 进行分类方面分别实现了卓越的区分度(AUC:0.927、0.897 和 0.899)。相应的紧凑模型保持了很强的辨别力(AUC:0.911、0.882 和 0.890),特征减少了 80.8%。相互作用模型产生了微妙的 AUC 变化(AUC:0.912、0.881 和 0.891),同时表征了潜在的临床联合效应模式。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该框架为临床实践中的同期风险分层生成了紧凑而透明的模型,将预测准确性与多级可解释性无缝结合起来。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架可以为开发用于 慢性乙型肝炎 患者风险分层的可解释人工智能工具提供信息,从而有可能改善临床决策和患者治疗结果。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 使用患者级数据分割、时间验证和独立外部验证以及校准和决策曲线分析来评估性能。提供的证据没有报告与研究设计或数据收集相关的具体限制。

papers.title: GAMBARAN HASIL PEMERIKSAAN ANTIBODI HEPATITIS B DAN HEPATITIS C PADA IBU HAMIL DENGAN METODE IMUNOKROMATOGRAFI DI PUSKESMAS SIDOARJO
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C are infectious diseases that can be transmitted from pregnant women to their babies during pregnancy, childbirth, or after birth. Screening examinations in pregnant women are important as an early detection effort to prevent vertical transmission. This study aimed to determine the profile of Hepatitis B antibody (HBsAb) and Hepatitis C antibody (Anti-HCV) test results among pregnant women using the immunochromatographic method at the Sidoarjo Community Health Center. This study employed a descriptive research design. The research was conducted at the Laboratory of the Sidoarjo Community Health Center from January to February 2026, involving 40 pregnant women who attended antenatal care (ANC) examinations. Testing was performed using the rapid immunochromatographic method on blood samples collected from the respondents to detect HBsAb and Anti-HCV antibodies. The results showed that, based on age, most respondents were in the 20–35 years age group, accounting for 32 individuals (80%). Based on gestational age, the majority of respondents were in the first trimester, totaling 22 individuals (55%). The HBsAb examination results indicated that 38 respondents (95%) were non-reactive and 2 respondents (5%) were reactive. Meanwhile, the Anti-HCV examination results showed that all 40 respondents (100%) were non-reactive. It is important for pregnant women to undergo Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C screening as a preventive measure to reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission. ABSTRAK Hepatitis B dan Hepatitis C merupakan penyakit infeksi yang beresiko menular dari ibu hamil kepada bayi selama kehamilan, persalinan, maupun setelah kelahiran. Pemeriksaan skrining pada ibu hamil penting dilakukan sebagai upaya deteksi dini untuk mencegah terjadinya penularan vertikal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui gambaran hasil pemeriksaan antibodi Hepatitis B (HBsAb) dan antibodi Hepatitis C (Anti-HCV) pada ibu hamil menggunakan metode imunokromatografi di Puskesmas Sidoarjo. Jenis penelitian yang digunakan adalah deskriptif. Penelitian dilakukan di Laboratorium Puskesmas Sidoarjo pada bulan Januari–Februari 2026 dengan jumlah responden sebanyak 40 ibu hamil yang melakukan pemeriksaan antenatal care (ANC). Pemeriksaan dilakukan menggunakan metode imunokromatografi rapid test terhadap sampel darah responden untuk mendeteksi HBsAb dan Anti-HCV. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa berdasarkan usia, sebagian besar responden berada pada kelompok usia 20–35 tahun sebanyak 32 orang (80%). Berdasarkan usia kehamilan, mayoritas responden berada pada trimester I sebanyak 22 orang (55%). Hasil pemeriksaan HBsAb menunjukkan sebanyak 38 responden (95%) non reaktif dan 2 responden (5%) reaktif. Sementara itu, hasil pemeriksaan Anti-HCV menunjukkan seluruh responden 40 orang (100%) non reaktif. Penting bagi ibu hamil untuk melakukan pemeriksaan Hepatitis B maupun Hepatitis C sebagai upaya pencegahan risiko penularan ibu hamil kepada bayi.

papers.title_zh: GAMBARAN HASIL PEMERIKSAAN 抗体 B 型肝炎 DAN 肝炎 C PADA IBU HAMIL DENGAN 方法免疫色谱法 DI PUSKESMAS SIDOARJO
papers.source_body_en: Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C are infectious diseases that can be transmitted from pregnant women to their babies during pregnancy, childbirth, or after birth. Screening examinations in pregnant women are important as an early detection effort to prevent vertical transmission. This study aimed to determine the profile of Hepatitis B antibody (HBsAb) and Hepatitis C antibody (Anti-HCV) test results among pregnant women using the immunochromatographic method at the Sidoarjo Community Health Center. This study employed a descriptive research design. The research was conducted at the Laboratory of the Sidoarjo Community Health Center from January to February 2026, involving 40 pregnant women who attended antenatal care (ANC) examinations. Testing was performed using the rapid immunochromatographic method on blood samples collected from the respondents to detect HBsAb and Anti-HCV antibodies. The results showed that, based on age, most respondents were in the 20–35 years age group, accounting for 32 individuals (80%). Based on gestational age, the majority of respondents were in the first trimester, totaling 22 individuals (55%). The HBsAb examination results indicated that 38 respondents (95%) were non-reactive and 2 respondents (5%) were reactive. Meanwhile, the Anti-HCV examination results showed that all 40 respondents (100%) were non-reactive. It is important for pregnant women to undergo Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C screening as a preventive measure to reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission. ABSTRAK Hepatitis B dan Hepatitis C merupakan penyakit infeksi yang beresiko menular dari ibu hamil kepada bayi selama kehamilan, persalinan, maupun setelah kelahiran. Pemeriksaan skrining pada ibu hamil penting dilakukan sebagai upaya deteksi dini untuk mencegah terjadinya penularan vertikal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui gambaran hasil pemeriksaan antibodi Hepatitis B (HBsAb) dan antibodi Hepatitis C (Anti-HCV) pada ibu hamil menggunakan metode imunokromatografi di Puskesmas Sidoarjo. Jenis penelitian yang digunakan adalah deskriptif. Penelitian dilakukan di Laboratorium Puskesmas Sidoarjo pada bulan Januari–Februari 2026 dengan jumlah responden sebanyak 40 ibu hamil yang melakukan pemeriksaan antenatal care (ANC). Pemeriksaan dilakukan menggunakan metode imunokromatografi rapid test terhadap sampel darah responden untuk mendeteksi HBsAb dan Anti-HCV. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa berdasarkan usia, sebagian besar responden berada pada kelompok usia 20–35 tahun sebanyak 32 orang (80%). Berdasarkan usia kehamilan, mayoritas responden berada pada trimester I sebanyak 22 orang (55%). Hasil pemeriksaan HBsAb menunjukkan sebanyak 38 responden (95%) non reaktif dan 2 responden (5%) reaktif. Sementara itu, hasil pemeriksaan Anti-HCV menunjukkan seluruh responden 40 orang (100%) non reaktif. Penting bagi ibu hamil untuk melakukan pemeriksaan Hepatitis B maupun Hepatitis C sebagai upaya pencegahan risiko penularan ibu hamil kepada bayi.

news.content_title: Advancing toward a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B: China's evolving role
news.content: Advanced Search Home News Releases Multimedia Meetings Login Register News Release 2-Nov-2026 Advancing toward a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B: China's evolving role New treatment strategies could help identify patients most likely to benefit from shorter courses of therapy Reports and Proceedings Chinese Medical Journals Publishing House Co., Ltd. Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email image: Chronic hepatitis B remains a major global health challenge, driving the search for more effective treatments. view more Credit: Dr. Zhujun Cao and Professor Qing Xie from Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China Image source link: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/poh2.70073?prg140729=e718ca3f-0104-4d08-b462-4fbdbf86e9fa Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a global health challenge and a leading cause of cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and liver cancer. Although vaccination and antiviral medicines have improved prevention and management, a lasting cure remains difficult. Current treatments suppress hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication, but many patients need long-term therapy. Developing treatments that maintain viral control after medication stops remains a research priority. China has made progress in preventing HBV infections through infant vaccination and measures to prevent mother-to-child transmission. However, approximately 75 million people in the country still live with chronic HBV infection. Against this backdrop, Dr. Zhujun Cao, Professor Qing Xie, and Dr. Dandan Weng from the Department of Infectious Diseases at Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China, examined China's contribution to developing treatments for CHB. Their perspective has been published online in Portal Hypertension & Cirrhosis journal on October 26, 2026. The authors examined published clinical trials, meta-analyses, national epidemiological surveys, and cohort studies. Their perspective considered established medicines, emerging treatments, safety, patient selection, and long-term outcomes in the pursuit of a functional cure. Existing antiviral medicines, including entecavir and tenofovir, can suppress HBV replication. However, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), a protein produced during infection, becomes undetectable in only around 2–5% of patients receiving long-term treatment. Pegylated interferon-α (PegIFNα), which stimulates the immune response against HBV, may help selected patients, particularly those with lower HBsAg levels before treatment. China-led studies, including the Everest Project and ANCHOR trial, reported encouraging results, although side effects and monitoring can limit wider use. One important development is bepirovirsen, which targets HBV RNA and reduces viral protein production. In the Phase III B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 trials, functional cure at week 72 was achieved by 20% and 19% of treated participants, respectively, compared with none in the placebo groups. Responses were more common among participants with lower HBsAg levels before treatment. However, approximately four in five treated participants did not achieve functional cure, and durability beyond reported follow-up remains uncertain. The trials excluded patients with cirrhosis, limiting how broadly the findings can be applied. “Although some emerging treatments can reduce viral markers, these changes do not necessarily lead to a lasting functional cure. Further research is needed to determine which approaches can maintain viral control after treatment stops,” shares Prof. Xie. Other treatments developed in China or evaluated with Chinese research participation target viral RNA, interfere with formation of the virus's protective protein shell, or stimulate immune responses. Some candidates have shown promising biological effects, while others have produced limited benefits or failed to meet their clinical objectives. Changes in viral markers do not always translate into lasting patient benefits. The authors highlight the need to tailor treatment to individual patients. HBsAg levels, viral activity, immune status, and liver damage may help identify who is most likely to benefit. Clinical registries and long-term follow-up could assess effectiveness, determine whether responses persist after treatment stops, and identify patients needing further care. Research involving underrepresented groups and populations with different HBV genotypes is also important. “The goal is not simply to provide more treatment, but to identify the right treatment intensity for each patient. Understanding who is most likely to benefit, while ensuring appropriate safety monitoring and follow-up, will be essential to developing more personalized approaches to CHB,” notes Dr. Cao. Overall, the perspective highlights progress in developing treatments for CHB while emphasizing that a safe, lasting functional cure remains out of reach for many patients. Further research is needed to determine which patients benefit most from emerging therapies, how long treatment responses persist, and whether these approaches can reduce serious complications such as cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and liver cancer. *** Reference DOI: 10.1002/poh2.70073 About Shanghai Jiao Tong University Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) is a leading public research university in Shanghai, China, with a history dating back to 1896. It is recognized for its academic excellence, research innovation, and contributions to science, engineering, medicine, and technology. The university offers a broad range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs and maintains collaborations with universities and research institutions worldwide. Its affiliated hospitals and medical schools contribute significantly to clinical research, biomedical sciences, and healthcare innovation. Through interdisciplinary research, advanced facilities, and international partnerships, SJTU plays an important role in China's higher education and global scientific research community. Website: https://en.sjtu.edu.cn/ About Professor Qing Xie from Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China Prof. Qing Xie is the Director of the Department of Infectious Diseases at Ruijin Hospital and Director of the Severe Viral Hepatitis Clinical Center at Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China. Her research focuses on the clinical management of hepatitis B and C, host immune responses to viral infections, liver injury, and liver fibrosis. She has led multicenter clinical trials involving viral hepatitis and established long-term clinical databases and sample banks for patients with hepatitis B and C. She has published over 100 research articles. About Dr. Zhujun Cao from Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China Dr. Zhujun Cao is a physician and researcher affiliated with the Department of Infectious Diseases at Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, China. His research focuses on hepatology and infectious diseases, particularly the mechanisms underlying organ failure in cirrhosis and the development of novel therapeutic approaches. He is involved in research on the immunopathogenesis of acute-on-chronic liver failure, using clinical research and multi-omics approaches to investigate disease mechanisms and identify potential therapeutic targets. Funding information This work was supported in part by the National Science and Technology Major Project of China (2025ZD01906200, Prevention and Control of Emerging and Major Infectious Diseases) and the National Ten Thousand Talents Program for Young Top-notch Talents. The other authors declare no conflicts of interest. No pharmaceutical companies developing HBV functional cure therapies provided research funding, consulting fees, speaker honoraria, or manuscript writing support for this perspective article. news.title_zh: 向 功能性治愈 for 慢性乙型肝炎 迈进:中国不断演变的角色 - EurekAlert!
news.source_body_en: This news report highlights China's advancements in the development of treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Published on November 2, 2026, by EurekAlert!, the article discusses research led by Dr. Zhujun Cao and Professor Qing Xie from Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine. The study, published in the Portal Hypertension & Cirrhosis journal on October 26, 2026, examines clinical trials, meta-analyses, and national epidemiological surveys to identify patients who may benefit from emerging therapies. China-led studies, including the Everest Project and ANCHOR trial, reported that 20% and 19% of treated participants achieved a functional cure at week 72, respectively, compared to none in the placebo groups. However, approximately 80% of treated participants did not achieve a functional cure, and the durability of these responses remains uncertain. The research emphasizes the need for personalized treatment approaches based on HBsAg levels, viral activity, immune status, and liver damage. The trials excluded patients with cirrhosis, limiting the generalizability of the findings. Further research is required to determine the optimal treatment intensity for individual patients and to ensure safety monitoring and follow-up. The article underscores the importance of understanding who benefits most from these therapies and how they can reduce serious complications like cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and liver cancer.
news.content_zh: 本新闻报道重点介绍了中国在制定 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 战略方面取得的进展。该文章于 2026 年 11 月 2 日由 EurekAlert! 发表,讨论了上海交通大学医学院曹竹君博士和谢庆教授领导的研究。该研究于 2026 年 10 月 26 日发表在《门脉高压和肝硬化》杂志上,研究了临床试验、荟萃分析和国家流行病学调查,以确定可能受益于新兴疗法的患者。中国主导的研究(包括珠穆朗玛峰项目和 ANCHOR 试验)报告称,接受治疗的参与者分别有 20% 和 19% 在第 72 周达到了 功能性治愈,而安慰剂组则没有。然而,大约 80% 的接受治疗的参与者没有达到 功能性治愈,并且这些反应的持久性仍不确定。该研究强调需要根据 HBsAg 水平、病毒活性、免疫状态和肝损伤采取个性化 治疗 方法。这些试验排除了肝硬化患者,限制了研究结果的普遍性。需要进一步的研究来确定个体患者的最佳 治疗 强度并确保安全监测和随访。该文章强调了了解谁从这些疗法中受益最多以及它们如何减少肝硬化、门静脉高压和肝癌等严重并发症的重要性。

Breakthrough: FDA Approves First Drug Offering a 'Functional Cure' For Chronic Hepatitis B Health05 November 2026 By David Nield (THOM LEACH/Science Photo Library RF/Getty Images) There's new hope for the millions of people affected by chronic hepatitis B (CHB), a liver condition that can lead to cancer, scarring, or organ failure, and which is responsible for over a million deaths worldwide each year. Following the results of two phase 3 clinical trials, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the drug bepirovirsen for CHB treatment, under the brand name Hibsago. GSK, the pharmaceutical company behind the drug's development, describes bepirovirsen as the first "functional cure" for CHB, meaning it doesn't just manage the virus causing the infection – as existing treatments do – but suppresses it to undetectable levels in the blood. What's more, in patients who respond, the infection stays under control even after bepirovirsen treatment is stopped, which is again in contrast to the drugs currently prescribed for CHB. "This is the start of a new era in treating people living with CHB," says gastroenterologist Norah Terrault, from the Keck Medical Center at the University of Southern California. "Bepirovirsen offers patients the potential to achieve functional cure after a short period of treatment, a long-standing goal for patients and physicians alike." frameborder="0′′ allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen> The phase 3 trial results showed that a six-month course of bepirovirsen achieved a functional cure response in 233 of 1,220 participants (19 percent), compared to 0 out of 614 participants on a placebo drug. In those patients, the virus stayed undetectable for at least 24 weeks after all treatment stopped (72 weeks after the trial began). The drug is administered via weekly injections and was given alongside existing pill treatments, which could then also be stopped for patients given the all-clear. "For the first time, with Hibsago, US patients have the potential to achieve functional cure after a six-month treatment course, with the added convenience of the option of self-administration after the first dose," says Tony Wood, Chief Scientific Officer at GSK, the pharmaceutical company developing the drug. Across two trials, bepirovirsen was effective in 233 of 1,220 patients. (Hou et al., N. Engl. J. Med., 2026) It's not all completely positive. Some patients did experience serious side effects, including liver inflammation, which the FDA says should be monitored for via regular blood tests. Traces of the virus do stick around, too – it's yet to be proven if the cure holds for years after treatment has ended. However, the improvements from current treatments are stark enough that the researchers are confident that a significant number of patients are going to benefit, and that's rubber-stamped by the FDA approval. "For many people living with chronic hepatitis B, treatment can mean taking antiviral medication for years to keep the virus suppressed," says Wendy Carter, the Acting Director at the FDA's Office of Infectious Diseases. "Hibsago provides a new treatment approach that gives some patients the possibility of maintaining control of the virus after all chronic HBV treatment has ended. This approval represents an important advance for people living with this serious disease." Some CHB patients responded better to bepirovirsen than others. Lower levels of a key CHB protein at the start of treatment – indicating a less active infection – meant a higher chance of the new drug working. That's something that could be tested for before bepirovirsen is prescribed. The work doesn't stop here. The researchers want to see how the new treatment might be combined with other drugs to become even more effective, and GSK wants to make it available to more patients worldwide. "CHB is a major public health challenge, affecting millions of people in the US and accounting for approximately 56 percent of all global liver cancer cases," says Chari Cohen, the President of the Hepatitis B Foundation. "Today marks significant progress towards our aim of transforming the way CHB is managed with improvements in screening, diagnosis, and the availability of innovative treatment options for our community." The results of the phase 3 clinical trials have been published in the New England Journal of Medicine. This article was fact-checked by Rebecca Dyer and edited by Rebecca Dyer. news.content_zh: 根据《新英格兰医学杂志》(N5、N26)发表的 3 期临床试验结果,美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 已批准贝匹罗韦森(商品名 Hibsago)作为第一个为 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 提供“功能性治愈”的药物。该药物将血液中的病毒抑制到不可检测的水平,并且在有反应的患者中,即使在 治疗 停止后也能保持病毒的控制(N9,N10)。它通过每周注射给药,可以与现有的 治疗 一起使用,允许一些患者停止服药 (N11)。然而,该疗法的长期有效性尚未得到证实,因为 治疗 (N16) 后病毒的痕迹可能会持续超过 24 周。FDA 指出,一些患者出现了严重的副作用,包括肝脏炎症,需要定期监测(N15)。此次批准标志着慢性乙型肝炎的治疗取得了重大进展,慢性乙型肝炎是一种影响全球数百万人的疾病,每年导致超过一百万人死亡(N4、N25)。

Send Close FDA News Share on Facebook Share on LinkedIn Share on X Email Article Copy Article Url Print NOVEMBER 2, 2026 FDA Approves Hibsago for Chronic HBV Infection Originally published by our sister publication Infectious Disease Special Edition By Meaghan Lee Callaghan The FDA has approved bepirovirsen (Hibsago, GSK) for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. The drug, a first-in-class antisense oligonucleotide, is approved for use in adult patients without cirrhosis who are receiving nucleoside/nucleotide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor therapy, who have suppressed HBV DNA, and with HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) levels at or less than 3,000 IU/mL, as determined by an FDA-authorized test. The approval, which was granted under FDA priority review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, follows positive phase 3 data. In the B-WELL phase 3 trials, the researchers found functional cure rates of 19% in adults with HBsAg levels at or less than 3,000 IU/mL taking bepirovirsen, compared with none of those on the current standard of care alone (N Engl J Med 2026;394[24]:2395-2406). Although a majority of patients in both arms reported experiencing adverse events, only 7% of patients in the bepirovirsen and 4% in the standard-of-care arms reported severe adverse events. “This is the start of a new era in treating people living with [chronic HBV],” study investigator Norah Terrault, MD, MPH, the chief of gastroenterology and hepatology at Keck Medicine of USC, in Los Angeles, said in a press release. “Bepirovirsen offers patients the potential to achieve functional cure after a short period of treatment, a long-standing goal for patients and physicians alike." Based on a GSK press release. analysis.location_and_population: The approval is relevant to adult patients without cirrhosis who are receiving nucleoside/nucleotide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor therapy, and have suppressed HBV DNA with HBsAg levels at or less than 3,000 IU/mL.
analysis.event: The FDA approved bepirovirsen (Hibsago) for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. This approval is based on positive phase 3 trial data.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In the B-WELL phase 3 trials, functional cure rates of 19% were observed in adults with HBsAg levels at or less than 3,000 IU/mL taking bepirovirsen, compared with none of those on the standard of care alone. Adverse events were reported by a majority of patients in both arms, but only 7% in the bepirovirsen group and 4% in the standard-of-care group experienced severe adverse events.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The drug is now available for eligible adults without cirrhosis. The findings are based on phase 3 trial data and are not subject to further investigation.

analysis.brief_en: The FDA has approved bepirovirsen (Hibsago) for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adult patients without cirrhosis who are receiving nucleoside/nucleotide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor therapy and have suppressed HBV DNA with HBsAg levels at or less than 3,000 IU/mL. This approval follows positive phase 3 trial data, which showed a 19% functional cure rate in patients treated with Hibsago, compared to none on the standard of care alone. Adverse events were reported by a majority of patients in both treatment groups, but only 7% in the Hibsago group and 4% in the standard-of-care group experienced severe adverse events. The approval was granted under FDA priority review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, marking a significant advancement in HBV treatment. The drug is now available for eligible patients, offering a potential functional cure after a short period of treatment.

news.source_body_en: The FDA has approved bepirovirsen (Hibsago) for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adult patients without cirrhosis who are receiving nucleoside/nucleotide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor therapy and have suppressed HBV DNA with HBsAg levels at or less than 3,000 IU/mL. The approval was granted under FDA priority review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, marking a significant advancement in HBV treatment. The drug is now available for eligible patients, offering a potential functional cure after a short period of treatment.

If you continue to have this issue please contact customerservice@slackinc.com . Key takeaways: People living with diabetes have increased risk for hepatitis B virus. Vaccination and screening are key to HBV prevention and early detection. Susan Weiner In this Diabetes in Real Life column, Susan Weiner, MS, RDN, CDN, CDCES, FADCES, talks with Arpan Mohanty, M D , MSc, about why hepatitis B warrants greater attention in diabetes care and what to know about vaccination, screening and more. Weiner: What is the clinical guidance for hepatitis vaccination for people living with diabetes? Mohanty: The American Diabetes Association recommends hepatitis B virus vaccination for all adults with diabetes younger than 60 years. For those aged 60 years or older, vaccination should be considered based on individual risk factors, such as exposure risk, living situation and other health conditions, consistent with Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices guidance. Weiner: What populations are at increased risk? Mohanty: Adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes have a higher risk for HBV . Among adults aged 19 to 59 years, the risk for acute infection is about twice that of people without diabetes. Diabetes may impair immune responses, reducing the likelihood of HBV clearance and increasing the risk for chronic infection. Risk may be especially high in long-term care settings or when blood glucose monitoring equipment is shared or not properly disinfected. In addition, vaccination is particularly important for people with diabetes, as they are more likely to develop metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), which can lead to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), cirrhosis or liver cancer. Preventing HBV with vaccination helps protect a liver that may already be vulnerable. Weiner: Describe the overlap of chronic kidney disease , diabetes, hypertension, inflammation and coordinated cardiometabolic management for people living with diabetes and hepatitis. Mohanty: In patients with diabetes, hepatitis or liver inflammation most commonly results from viral infection, alcohol-associated liver disease or MASH, the inflammatory form of MASLD. MASLD and MASH frequently coexist with obesity, hypertension, dyslipidemia and CKD and should be viewed within the broader cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. These conditions share common drivers, including insulin resistance, excess adiposity, endothelial dysfunction and chronic systemic inflammation. The relationship between MASLD and type 2 diabetes is bidirectional: Type 2 diabetes increases the risk for MASLD progression while MASLD may worsen insulin resistance and glycemic control. Consequently, MASLD, particularly when fibrosis is present, is associated not only with liver-related outcomes, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, but also with a higher risk for major adverse cardiovascular events. Management should therefore be coordinated, rather than organ-specific. Therapies selected to improve glycemic control and protect the heart and kidneys may also reduce liver fat or injury while newer liver-directed treatments can slow or potentially reverse fibrosis in patients with MASH. Viral hepatitis also warrants prompt treatment. Hepatitis C virus cure may improve glycemic control and is associated with reduced kidney and CV complications. A coordinated CKM-liver strategy can therefore address shared risk factors while improving outcomes across the liver, heart and kidneys. Weiner: Dialysis populations have historically experienced higher rates of HBV exposure. What enhanced infection control measures and monitoring situations should be implemented? Mohanty: Patients receiving hemodialysis remain at increased risk for HBV and HCV because of frequent blood exposure, shared treatment environments and impaired immune function, which increases susceptibility to infection and reduces vaccine responsiveness. Prevention should begin before admission to an outpatient dialysis unit. The CDC recommends baseline testing with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), antibody to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) for all patients starting hemodialysis. Susceptible patients should be vaccinated as early as possible, ideally before dialysis begins. For patients vaccinated after dialysis initiation, higher-dose regimens are recommended, followed by anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months after series completion. Patients who do not achieve protective immunity should receive a second vaccine series. Ongoing HBV surveillance should be guided by immune status. Patients who remain susceptible should undergo monthly HBsAg testing, whereas vaccine responders should have anti-HBs levels checked annually and be revaccinated if titers fall below 10 IU/L. Patients with immunity from prior infection generally do not require additional routine HBV testing. In addition, patients should also be screened for HCV at dialysis initiation and every 6 months thereafter. Screening for viral hepatitis is also important when transferring to another dialysis center or changing treatment type, after a blood exposure, and whenever a new HBV case is identified in the unit. Infection control within the dialysis unit is equally important. Standard precautions, meticulous hand hygiene, appropriate use of personal protective equipment, safe medication and injection practices, disinfection of dialysis stations and shared equipment, and maintenance of water quality should be consistently enforced. Patients who test positive for HbsAg should be promptly isolated and dialyzed using dedicated equipment, with unit-specific exposure protocols implemented to reduce transmission. Weiner: How can hepatitis be prevented, detected and treated in the diabetes population? Which members of the healthcare team should support these efforts? Mohanty: Hepatitis prevention, detection and referral for treatment should be integrated into routine diabetes care. The key steps are to assess vaccination status, complete recommended screening and ensure timely follow-up of positive results. Prevention begins with HBV vaccination. The ADA Standards of Care recommend vaccination for adults with diabetes aged younger than 60 years and individualized vaccination for those aged 60 years or older. Vaccine response may be reduced by older age, obesity, CKD, immunosuppression and diabetes itself. The two-dose CpG-adjuvanted vaccine (Heplisav-B, Dynavax) provides higher seroprotection and a shorter completion interval than conventional three-dose regimens. Postvaccination serologic testing is important when confirmation of immunity is clinically necessary, including for patients receiving hemodialysis, immunocompromised individuals and healthcare personnel. Detection has been simplified by universal adult screening. All adults should undergo HBV screening at least once with HbsAg, anti-HBs and total anti-HBc, as well as one-time HCV antibody testing with reflex RNA testing. Repeat testing is indicated for those with ongoing risk. In diabetes care, the operational priority is to confirm that screening has been completed, document the results and establish a reliable follow-up pathway. Patients with positive results should be referred promptly. Chronic HBV can be effectively suppressed, and HCV is curable in most patients, including those with advanced CKD. HCV cure may also improve glycemic control and reduce kidney and CV complications. Antiviral selection and monitoring may intersect with renal function, lipid management and glucose-lowering therapy. The optimal model for hepatitis prevention and treatment often requires coordinated, interprofessional care, which depends on the clinical context and institutional resources. Primary care clinicians and endocrinologists can assess vaccination and screening status and initiate referrals while nurses, medical assistant and pharmacists can use standing orders, administer vaccines and track series completion. Diabetes care and education specialists can reinforce the relevance of hepatitis to diabetes outcomes; nephrology and dialysis teams can oversee dialysis-specific surveillance and infection control; and hepatology or infectious disease specialists can screen for hepatitis, manage confirmed infection and advanced liver disease. Each institution should establish a clear coordination point, assign responsibility for each step and embed hepatitis care within the diabetes pathway to prevent incomplete vaccination, missed results and unclosed referrals. Weiner: How can we improve prevention, detection and treatment in underserved and at-risk communities? Mohanty: Improving hepatitis prevention and care in underserved communities requires embedding services in the settings where people with diabetes already receive care, including primary care, endocrinology, pharmacies, dialysis units and diabetes education programs. Each setting should first identify its implementation gaps, such as low vaccination rates, incomplete screening or loss to follow-up, assess their magnitude and local causes, and tailor interventions accordingly. Strategies to improve vaccination and screening include standing vaccination orders, opt-out testing and electronic health record prompts, which can reduce missed opportunities and help address disparities. Testing should also be available beyond traditional clinics through community health centers, mobile programs, shelters, correctional facilities, syringe-service programs and other settings that reach people with limited access to care. Treatment access can be expanded through telehealth and task-shifting. Primary care clinicians, nurse practitioners and other trained nonspecialists can treat uncomplicated HCV with specialist support, allowing hepatology resources to focus on patients with cirrhosis, complex coinfection or treatment failure. Telehealth and Project ECHO (Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes)-type models can extend expertise to rural and safety-net settings, although telephone-based options may be needed for patients with limited internet access. Finally, improving outcomes requires addressing barriers that commonly interrupt care, including transportation, insurance coverage, medication costs, housing instability, limited health literacy and stigma. Community health workers, peer navigators, social workers and culturally and linguistically tailored education can help patients move from screening to treatment without being lost to follow-up. The most effective approach is a coordinated, context-specific system that combines easier access, automated workflows, community partnerships and clear ownership of follow-up. Weiner: Is there current research available on other hepatitis treatments? Mohanty: Research in MASH treatment is advancing rapidly, an especially important development for people with type 2 diabetes who are at high risk for MASLD/MASH and resultant progressive liver fibrosis. Resmetirom (Rezdiffra, Madrigal Pharmaceuticals), a thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist, and semaglutide (Wegovy, Novo Nordisk), a GLP-1 receptor agonist, are now FDA-approved for adults with noncirrhotic MASH and moderate to advanced fibrosis, in conjunction with lifestyle modification. Incretin-based therapies remain particularly relevant to diabetes care. Phase 2 trials of tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound, Eli Lilly) and survodutide (Boehringer Ingelheim) have shown improvements in MASH, weight and cardiometabolic risk. Fibroblast growth factor 21, or FGF21, analogs, including efruxifermin (Novo Nordisk) and pegozafermin (Roche), have also shown promising effects on liver fibrosis and metabolic parameters and are now being evaluated in phase 3 trials. These advances also reinforce the importance of identifying fibrosis early so eligible patients can benefit from approved therapies or clinical trials. For more information: Arpan Mohanty, M D , MSc, is a hepatologist at Boston Medical Center and assistant professor of medicine at Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine. Partager cet article The new drug submission for bepirovirsen was granted priority review, underscoring the unmet need for patients Submission supported by statistically significant and clinically meaningful functional cure rates in pivotal Phase III B-Well trials An estimated 262,000 people in Canada live with chronic hepatitis B, a leading cause of liver cancer1 MISSISSAUGA, ON, April 30, 2026 /CNW/ - GSK today announced that it has filed a new drug submission for bepirovirsen for regulatory review in Canada. Bepirovirsen is an investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) for the treatment of adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The submission will be reviewed under the Health Canada priority review policy. Chronic hepatitis B remains a public health concern in Canada, with an estimated 262,000 people living with CHB.1 The current standard of care--nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy--typically requires lifelong treatment, and rates of functional cure remain very low, at approximately 1%.2 A functional cure is defined as undetectable hepatitis B virus DNA and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in the blood for at least 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, indicating that the disease is controlled by the immune system without medication.3 Globally, CHB is estimated to cause roughly 56% of liver cancer cases. 4 "CHB imposes a significant burden on patients, increasing the risk of liver cancer and other serious liver disease. In Canada, these risks are exacerbated by inequities in screening, access to quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen testing, and connection to care," said Dr. Michelle Horn, Country Medical Director, GSK Canada. "The priority review of bepirovirsen is an important milestone in our efforts to transform care for people living with chronic hepatitis B." Positive Phase III results from the B‐Well 1 and B‐Well 2 trials support the regulatory submission for bepirovirsen. Bepirovirsen plus standard of care produced statistically significant and clinically meaningful functional cure rates versus standard of care alone across all ranked endpoints. The trials demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile consistent with what was reported in other studies. The data is planned for presentation at the European Association for the Study of Liver Congress (EASL) and submission to a peer‐reviewed journal later this year. The priority review designation in Canada reflects bepirovirsen's innovation and potential to address a disease with high unmet medical need. Bepirovirsen's safety and effectiveness are still under investigation, and market authorization has not yet been granted in Canada or any other country. The Canadian regulatory submission follows earlier filings in Japan, China, the European Union, and the United States. In the United States, bepirovirsen received Breakthrough Therapy designation from the Food and Drug Administration. About chronic hepatitis B Hepatitis B is a viral infection that can cause both acute and chronic liver disease. Chronic hepatitis B occurs when the immune system is unable to clear the virus, resulting in long-lasting infection that affects an estimated 262,000 people in Canada. The disease causes approximately 1.1 million deaths each year globally.1 Many patients require lifelong antiviral therapy for viral suppression, making functional cure a critical goal in disease management. The Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver (CASL) and the Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada (AMMI) updated guidelines identify functional cure as the ultimate goal of treatment.5 About bepirovirsen Bepirovirsen is a triple action investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), designed to recognise and orchestrate the destruction of the genetic components (i.e. mRNA and pregenomic RNA) of the hepatitis B virus that can lead to chronic disease. Bepirovirsen inhibits the replication of the viral genome in the body and suppresses the level of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in the blood. Bepirovirsen also has innate immunostimulatory activity which may contribute to its therapeutic effect. About B-Well Clinical trial programmes B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 trials are global multi-centre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials conducted in 29 countries. They assessed the efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetic profile, and the durability of functional cure in nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA)-treated participants with CHB and baseline surface antigen (HBsAg) ≤3000 IU/ml. The primary endpoint assessed the proportion of participants achieving functional cure in patients with baseline surface antigen (HBsAg) ≤3000 IU/ml. Functional cure was defined as sustained suppression (24 weeks or longer) of HBV DNA (<LLOQ) and HBsAg not detected, with or without hepatitis B surface antibodies, after a finite duration of therapy with bepirovirsen and off all HBV treatment. Partager cet article The new drug submission for bepirovirsen was granted priority review, underscoring the unmet need for patients Submission supported by statistically significant and clinically meaningful functional cure rates in pivotal Phase III B-Well trials An estimated 262,000 people in Canada live with chronic hepatitis B, a leading cause of liver cancer1 MISSISSAUGA, ON, April 30, 2026 /CNW/ - GSK today announced that it has filed a new drug submission for bepirovirsen for regulatory review in Canada. Bepirovirsen is an investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) for the treatment of adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The submission will be reviewed under the Health Canada priority review policy. Chronic hepatitis B remains a public health concern in Canada, with an estimated 262,000 people living with CHB.1 The current standard of care--nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy--typically requires lifelong treatment, and rates of functional cure remain very low, at approximately 1%.2 A functional cure is defined as undetectable hepatitis B virus DNA and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in the blood for at least 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, indicating that the disease is controlled by the immune system without medication.3 Globally, CHB is estimated to cause roughly 56% of liver cancer cases. 4 "CHB imposes a significant burden on patients, increasing the risk of liver cancer and other serious liver disease. In Canada, these risks are exacerbated by inequities in screening, access to quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen testing, and connection to care," said Dr. Michelle Horn, Country Medical Director, GSK Canada. "The priority review of bepirovirsen is an important milestone in our efforts to transform care for people living with chronic hepatitis B." Positive Phase III results from the B‐Well 1 and B‐Well 2 trials support the regulatory submission for bepirovirsen. Bepirovirsen plus standard of care produced statistically significant and clinically meaningful functional cure rates versus standard of care alone across all ranked endpoints. The trials demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile consistent with what was reported in other studies. The data is planned for presentation at the European Association for the Study of Liver Congress (EASL) and submission to a peer‐reviewed journal later this year. The priority review designation in Canada reflects bepirovirsen's innovation and potential to address a disease with high unmet medical need. Bepirovirsen's safety and effectiveness are still under investigation, and market authorization has not yet been granted in Canada or any other country. The Canadian regulatory submission follows earlier filings in Japan, China, the European Union, and the United States. In the United States, bepirovirsen received Breakthrough Therapy designation from the Food and Drug Administration. About chronic hepatitis B Hepatitis B is a viral infection that can cause both acute and chronic liver disease. Chronic hepatitis B occurs when the immune system is unable to clear the virus, resulting in long-lasting infection that affects an estimated 262,000 people in Canada. The disease causes approximately 1.1 million deaths each year globally.1 Many patients require lifelong antiviral therapy for viral suppression, making functional cure a critical goal in disease management. The Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver (CASL) and the Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada (AMMI) updated guidelines identify functional cure as the ultimate goal of treatment.5 About bepirovirsen Bepirovirsen is a triple action investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), designed to recognise and orchestrate the destruction of the genetic components (i.e. mRNA and pregenomic RNA) of the hepatitis B virus that can lead to chronic disease. Bepirovirsen inhibits the replication of the viral genome in the body and suppresses the level of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in the blood. Bepirovirsen also has innate immunostimulatory activity which may contribute to its therapeutic effect. About B-Well Clinical trial programmes B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 trials are global multi-centre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials conducted in 29 countries. They assessed the efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetic profile, and the durability of functional cure in nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA)-treated participants with CHB and baseline surface antigen (HBsAg) ≤3000 IU/ml. The primary endpoint assessed the proportion of participants achieving functional cure in patients with baseline surface antigen (HBsAg) ≤3000 IU/ml. Functional cure was defined as sustained suppression (24 weeks or longer) of HBV DNA (<LLOQ) and HBsAg not detected, with or without hepatitis B surface antibodies, after a finite duration of therapy with bepirovirsen and off all HBV treatment. GSK licensed bepirovirsen from Ionis Pharmaceuticals and collaborated with them on its development. Bepirovirsen is currently not approved anywhere in the world. A breakthrough therapy designation (BTD) in the United States enables greater FDA guidance on an asset's development programme.6 The BTD for bepirovirsen builds on the Fast Track Designation also provided by the US FDA in February 2024. A Fast Track Designation expedites the review of drugs to treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need. analysis_en.time: April 30, 2026 /CNW/ - GSK today announced that it has filed a new drug submission for bepirovirsen for regulatory review in Canada.
